description: 1. List the Huawei Cloud ECS (Elastic Cloud Server) instances of a tenant region through KooCLI (`hcloud ECS ListServersDetails`, the official read-only GET /v1/{project_id}/cloudservers/detail), with an automatic fallback to the official huaweicloudsdkecs v2 SDK (EcsClient.list_servers_details) when hcloud is not installed. 2. Export the instance list into a well-formed local Markdown table (headers 名称 / ID / 状态 / 规格 / vCPU / 内存 / 可用区 / 私网IP / 公网IP, missing fields render `-`, optional summary line) — strictly local file generation, nothing is ever written back to the cloud. `--output` sets the path (default `ecs_instances_<region>_<timestamp>.md`); the parent directory is created automatically and the file is written via a temp file + atomic rename. 3. Three output modes: `--format md` (default) / `table` / `json`. Region aware: `--region` (default cn-north-4). Optional `--status` / `--name` server-side filters and `--page-size` (default 100); paging follows the reported `count`. 4. Explicit error classification: missing AK/SK credentials (「缺少 AK/SK 凭证」), hcloud not installed (falls back to SDK, else a clear hint), invalid/insufficient credentials (403 / 401 → IAM hint), KooCLI usage errors, and generic API/network failures. Empty instance lists produce a friendly hint and never a corrupt Markdown file. 5. Built-in write-intent guard: any mutating intent (create / delete / update / reboot / resize / attach / detach / start / stop …) or any operation other than the read-only ListServersDetails is rejected before execution — this skill is strictly read-only. 6. Triggers include: "查询 ECS 生成 Markdown", "ECS 实例列表导出 Markdown", "ecs markdown", "导出 ECS 实例为 Markdown 文件", "ECS 实例报表", "云服务器清单 Markdown", "ECS instance list markdown", "export ECS instances to markdown", "ecs 报表". 7. Offline unit tests (mocked hcloud subprocess) cover output modes, paging, Markdown format correctness, filters, empty lists, error classification, the SDK fallback, the extra-args injection position, the skill-quality-cli wrapper and the write-intent guard.
